t: garments. For the definition of a garment see below, halakhah 11.
and sacks. See below, halakhah 12.
and bone utensils. Utensils made from the bones of animals.
it says, "of any wooden vessel, or garment, or skin, or sack". All these become impure when a creeping animal falls on them.

and regarding metal vessels it says, "Only the gold and the silver". In the war against Midian the Israelites were commanded to purify the metal vessels they took as spoil, which shows that they receive impurity.

and regarding earthenware vessels it says, "and any earthenware vessel into which any of them falls". That a creeping animal makes an earthenware vessel impure by entering its airspace (below 13:1). The same applies to all impurities, since all are learned from one another through the rules by which the Torah is expounded (Commentary to the Mishnah, Kelim 2:1).
